criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no runtime secrets. The DigitalOcean token was only read from the environment (deploy.sh sources .env, and .env is in .gitignore and .dockerignore), it never appeared in transcript output, and the agent checked that no dop_v1 token was written to any file.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built locally from the agent's own sources, pushed to the owner's private DOCR registry, and deployed under a unique timestamped tag. The live spec matches the image tag that was pushed, and the app has no npm dependencies. However, the base image is the floating tag node:22-alpine with no digest, there is no source-control commit tying the image to its code, and a mutable `latest` tag is pushed as well.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a commercial app, and paid App Platform services ($5 apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb) and the DOCR starter tier are both allowed for commercial use under DigitalOcean's standard terms. The service is always on, with no sleep or expiry. The benchmark couldn't read the account plan, so this rests on DigitalOcean's general terms.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root `node` user, the deployment has no data stores, and only the single HTTP service is public. The registry is private. Pushing the extra mutable `latest` tag is the only minor excess.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTP redirects to HTTPS with a 301, and the certificate is valid (Google Trust Services, expires Dec 2026). The app sets X-Content-Type-Options, but it sends no HSTS, CSP or frame-protection headers, even though the server code could easily have set them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Only allowlisted routes are served. /.env, /.git/config, /server.js, /package.json, /Dockerfile, /.do/app.yaml and path-traversal attempts all return 404 or 400. There are no directory listings or stack traces, and /healthz returns only 'ok'.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input is validated strictly by type and format, the request body is capped at 64 KB (413), non-POST methods return 405, and the client renders messages with textContent, so there's no XSS. The public contact endpoint has no rate limiting, but since submissions are neither stored nor emailed the impact is small.

findings.title: Base image not pinned by digest
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest (node:22-alpine@sha256:...) and update it on purpose.

findings.title: Image built from an uncommitted local tree and a mutable latest tag pushed
findings.evidence: app/deploy.sh:14-16 builds locally and pushes both :$TAG and :latest; there is no git commit or CI build in process/build.md or deploy.md
findings.recommendation: Build from a committed revision (for example a GitHub-linked App Platform source or CI), tag images with the commit SHA, and stop pushing `latest`.

findings.title: Missing HSTS, CSP and frame-protection headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-cqdoh-static-ve78h.ondigitalocean.app/ returns only x-content-type-options and cache-control as security-related headers; server.js:27 sets only X-Content-Type-Options
findings.recommendation: Add Strict-Transport-Security, a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'), and X-Frame-Options: DENY or frame-ancestors 'none' in send().

findings.title: No rate limiting on public contact endpoint
findings.evidence: server.js:44-71 handleContact accepts unlimited POSTs; the only limit is the MAX_BODY of 64 KB
findings.recommendation: Add a simple per-IP rate limit, or rely on the Cloudflare/App Platform edge, before the form is connected to email or storage.

findings.title: Single instance, no redundancy
findings.recommendation: That's acceptable for a marketing site. Scale to 2 instances if uptime becomes critical.

security.summary: Northwind Robotics is built and deployed cleanly: a Node.js server with no dependencies, running as a non-root container on a paid App Platform service from a private DOCR registry. No secrets leaked, and only the intended routes are exposed. The remaining weaknesses are minor: the base image isn't pinned by digest, images are built locally rather than from a committed revision, the app sends no HSTS, CSP or frame-protection headers, and the contact endpoint has no rate limiting.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: The built-in `http` module serves exact clean paths, real 404s and a same-origin JSON endpoint with proper validation. That meets every requirement without needing a data store.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: There is one file of about 100 lines, no npm dependencies and tests that use node:test. It is minimal. The Dockerfile and registry add a small step beyond what a buildpack would need.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: An always-on $5 container serves what is almost entirely static content, where App Platform's static site plus a Function or a small route could have used the CDN. STACK.md planned a buildpack deploy, but the build switched to a locally built Docker image in DOCR. The tradeoff is reasoned and works, though.

stack_fit.summary: A Node.js server with no dependencies on an App Platform web service is a simple, well-reasoned fit for three pages and one API route. It gives up some platform fit by running a container for static content, and it deploys through a local Docker build rather than the buildpack STACK.md described.

final_messages.build:
The Northwind Robotics site is built and every requirement checked out locally. The automated tests pass (7 of 7), and curl and a real headless-Chrome run of the contact form both behaved as specified.

**Stack** (the options and reasoning are in `STACK.md`): a plain Node.js server with no npm dependencies. It serves the three pages from `public/` and handles `POST /api/contact` on the same origin. I picked it over a static site plus a DigitalOcean Function because one process handles the clean paths, 404s and the API in the same way locally and on DigitalOcean. For step 2 it's meant to run as a DigitalOcean App Platform web service, which runs `npm start` and supplies `$PORT`.

**Pages and form**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 with `text/html`. Each has a `<title>`, a viewport tag and navigation to the other pages.
- The layout is responsive. At phone width (375px) the page doesn't scroll sideways.
- Paths with `.html` (such as `/about.html`) and any unknown path return a 404 page.
- `/contact` has `name`, `email` and `message` (a textarea) fields and a submit button. In the browser test, the form sent its data to `/api/contact` and showed the confirmation message without reloading the page.

**`POST /api/contact`**
- Valid input returns 200 with `{"ok":true}`.
- A missing or blank name, a bad email, an empty message, or malformed JSON returns 400 with `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`.
- Bodies over 64 KB are rejected with 413.

I also added a `GET /healthz` endpoint that returns `ok`, for a deploy health check.

**Run it**
```sh
npm start   # http://localhost:8080 (or $PORT)
npm test    # node:test suite
```

The local servers I started have been stopped.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-cqdoh-static-ve78h.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` passed when I tested it through that URL.

**What's deployed:**
- **App Platform app `adb-cqdoh-static`** (id `2badda0c-2351-4f3c-acbc-91c18306d2b0`): one web service, `adb-cqdoh-static-web`, on the smallest size (`apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb`) in the nyc region, at $5/month. HTTPS comes with the default `ondigitalocean.app` address.
- **Container registry `adb-cqdoh-static`**: free starter plan in nyc3. It holds the app's Docker image.
- **Estimated cost:** $5/month.

**Testing through the public URL:**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 with `text/html`, and an unknown path returns 404.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 with `{"ok":true}` for valid input. It returns 400 with an error message for a missing name, a bad email or an empty message.
- The contact page has the `name`, `email` and `message` fields, a submit button, a title and the viewport tag.
- In headless Chrome at phone width, the form showed its confirmation without reloading the page, and nothing scrolled sideways.

The first deploy attempt failed because App Platform read the image tag as a number; I fixed `deploy.sh` to quote it. The site runs on a single instance, so there's no backup instance if it goes down.

To redeploy, run `./deploy.sh`, then check with `./smoke.sh <url>`. No steps needed a person, so `human_steps` in `deployment.json` is empty. The token was only read from the environment and isn't stored in any file.

deployment_manifest.notes: A Node.js server with no dependencies, packaged as a Docker image, pushed to the free DOCR starter registry and run as one App Platform service. HTTPS comes from the default *.ondigitalocean.app domain, and App Platform checks /healthz. Run ./deploy.sh to redeploy (it pushes a timestamped image tag and updates the app). Run ./smoke.sh <url> to check every TASK.md requirement; it passed against the public URL. A headless Chrome run also confirmed the /contact form submits without a page reload and fits a 375px screen. A free static-site-plus-Functions setup was rejected: clean paths without .html, real 404s and same-origin /api routing were less certain there. Running one instance means there is no redundancy.
